title: Controversies after Luther: Providence — three Lutheran grounds that the Reformed make God author of sin
pass_a_gloss: CONTROVERSIES BORN AFTER LUTHER. On God Providence, Predestination, & annexed heads. III. I. On God as author namely of Sin as constituted by the Reformed, namely 1. From the will of εὐδοκία / permissive good-pleasure, so lucidly asserted by Luther, the ingenuous Sons not denying it; 2. From hypothetical necessity or of futurition & of the event, flowing from infallible πρόγνωσις, and also from the necessity of immutability which Luther pressed most sharply, from God immutable & unsearchable good-pleasure, counsel, will, disposition; even in Pharaoh hardening, Judas betrayal, &c. 3. From the mode of the same Providence, least idle or ineffective (they call it Concurrence) around actions infected by sin, as they are actions, necessary again to Luther himself, though not by necessity of compulsion, Book On the Bondage of the Will pp. 67–68, &c.
pass_b_english: CONTROVERSIES BORN AFTER LUTHER. On God's Providence, Predestination, and the heads annexed to them.

III. First: whether the Reformed make God the author of Sin — namely (1) from the will of εὐδοκία, that is of permissive good-pleasure, which Luther asserted so clearly that his own candid sons do not deny it; (2) from a hypothetical necessity, or necessity of futurition and of the event, flowing from infallible foreknowledge (πρόγνωσις), and also from that necessity of immutability which Luther pressed hardest, drawn from God's immutable and unsearchable good-pleasure, counsel, will, and disposition — even in the hardening of Pharaoh, the betrayal of Judas, and the like; (3) from the mode of that same Providence, least idle or ineffective (they call it Concurrence) around actions infected by sin, as actions, which again Luther himself treats as necessary, though not by a necessity of compulsion — On the Bondage of the Will, pages 67–68, and so on.
source_text: CONTROVERSIAE POST LUTHERUM NATAE. De Providentia Dei, Praedestinatione, & Annexis Capitibus. III. I. De Deo auctore scilicet Peccati a Reformatis constituto, nempe 1. Ex voluntate εὐδοκίας seu beneplaciti permissivi, a Luthero tam luculenter asserti, non negantibus Filiis ingenuis; 2. Ex necessitate hypothetica seu futuritionis & eventûs, fluente ex infallibili προγνώσει, tùm & necessitate immutabilitatis quam ursit acerrimè Lutherus, ex immutabili ac imperescrutabili Dei beneplacito, consilio, voluntate, dispositione; etiam in Induratione Pharaonis, Proditione Judae, &c. 3. Ex modo Providentiae ejusdem, minimè otiosae aut inefficacis, (Concursum vocant) circa actiones peccato infectas, ut actiones sunt, necessarias rursum ipsi Luthero, quamvis non necessitate coactionis, Libro de Servo Arbitr. p. 67. 68. &c.
